# Tobit Chapter 10 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** Meanwhile, his father Tobit was counting every day. When the days of the journey were fulfilled and they had not returned, Tobit said,

**10:2** "Perhaps he has been delayed? Or perhaps Gabael has died and there is no one to give him the money?"

**10:3** He grew heavy with grief. His wife Anna said, "My boy has perished — he is no longer among the living." And she began to weep and wail for her son,

**10:4** saying, "Woe is me, my child, that I let you go — you who are the light of my eyes!"

**10:5** Tobit said to her, "Hush. Do not be troubled; he is well."

**10:6** She said to him, "Be silent yourself! Do not deceive me. My child has perished." She went out every day onto the road by which he had traveled, watching all day long, and stopped only to eat. At night she never ceased her lamentation for her son Tobias.

**10:7** When the fourteen days of the wedding feast that Raguel had sworn for his daughter had passed, Tobias came to him and said, "Send me away, for I know that my father and mother no longer believe they will see me again. Now I beg you, father, let me depart so that I may go to my father; I have already told you in what state I left him."

**10:8** Raguel said to Tobias, "Stay with me, and I will send word to your father about how you are faring." Tobias said, "No — please, send me to my father."

**10:9** So Raguel arose and gave him his wife Sarah, along with half of all his possessions: male servants and female servants, cattle and donkeys and sheep, clothing and money and household goods.

**10:10** He sent them off safely and embraced Tobias, saying, "Farewell, my child; travel safely. May the Lord of heaven grant you and your wife Sarah well-being, and may I see your children before I die."

**10:11** To his daughter Sarah he said, "Go to your father-in-law; from now on they are your parents, as those who gave you birth. Go in peace, my daughter; may I hear good news of you for as long as I live." He kissed her and sent her on her way.

**10:12** Edna said to Tobias, "My child — dear brother — may the Lord bring you back safely, and may I see children born of my daughter Sarah before I die. Before the Lord I entrust my daughter to you. Do not cause her grief all the days of your life. Go in peace, my child. From now on I am your mother and Sarah is your sister. May we all prosper together all the days of our lives." And she kissed him.

**10:13** Tobias set out from Raguel joyful and in good health, blessing the Lord of heaven and earth, the King of all, because he had made his journey prosper. And he blessed them as they departed until they drew near to Nineveh.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 10 divides into two movements: Anna's grief in Nineveh (vv. 1-6) and the farewell scene at Ecbatana (vv. 7-13). Deliberations focused on: the register of Anna's grief and her sharp retort (v. 6), the farewell speeches (vv. 10-12), and the final verse's transition.

LOGOS provides the structural base throughout. PNEUMA's emotional sharpness is adopted in a few specific places where the Greek's directness calls for it (notably v. 3's "My boy has perished" over EMET's more distanced "The boy has perished"). EMET's preservation of the full goods inventory (v. 9) and Anna's nighttime vigil detail (v. 6) is followed by all three agents.

On verse 13: EMET's bracketed last clause and LOGOS/PNEUMA's smoother integration both reflect the Sinaiticus text. SOPHIA normalizes "and he blessed them as they departed" rather than the redundant "And he said to him… And they departed."

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA Resolution |
|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|-------------------|
| 10:1 | Opening temporal marker | No "Meanwhile" | "Meanwhile" added | "Back home" added | "Meanwhile" — LOGOS; orientates reader without editorializing |
| 10:3 | Anna's declaration | "The boy has perished" | "My boy has perished" | "Our boy is dead. He's not coming back" | "My boy has perished" — LOGOS (personal "My" from Greek ho pais mou); PNEUMA's two-sentence split adds to the text |
| 10:3 | Grief description | "was grieved in-soul" | "grew heavy with grief" | "grief settled over him like a weight" | "grew heavy with grief" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's simile adds imagery not in the Greek |
| 10:4 | Anna's cry | "O woe to-me, child" | "Woe is me, my child" | "Oh, my child! Why did I let you go?" | "Woe is me, my child" — LOGOS; PNEUMA restructures into question form not in the text |
| 10:5 | Tobit's response | "Be-silent!" | "Hush." | "Hush." | "Hush." — LOGOS/PNEUMA agreement; more natural than EMET's "Be silent!" |
| 10:6 | Anna's retort | "Be-silent yourself! Do not deceive me." | "Be silent yourself! Do not deceive me." | "Don't tell me to be quiet. Don't try to fool me." | "Be silent yourself! Do not deceive me." — LOGOS; PNEUMA's colloquial register is slightly too modern |
| 10:7 | Tobias's address to Raguel | "I beg you, father, let me depart" | "I beg you, father, let me depart" | "Please, father — let me go back" | EMET/LOGOS agreement: "I beg you, father, let me depart" — preserves the formal petition |
| 10:9 | Inventory structure | Full hyphenated list | Full list | Abbreviated ("the servants, the livestock…") | Full list preserved (EMET/LOGOS) — the itemization has legal and narrative weight |
| 10:10 | Physical farewell | "he embraced Tobias" | "he embraced Tobias" | "threw his arms around Tobias" | "embraced Tobias" — LOGOS/EMET; PNEUMA adds physical specificity not in the Greek verb |
| 10:11 | Address to Sarah | "daughter" throughout | "my daughter" | "my darling girl" | "my daughter" — LOGOS; adds warmth without PNEUMA's sentimentality |
| 10:12 | Edna's charge | "Do not cause-her-grief all the days-of your-life" | "Do not cause her grief all the days of your life" | "Do not ever make her cry" | "Do not cause her grief all the days of your life" — LOGOS/EMET; PNEUMA's "make her cry" loses the range of lupe (grief, not just tears) |
| 10:13 | Closing transition | Bracketed scribal note | Smooth integration | Paraphrase ("full heart") | Normalized with LOGOS base; "he blessed them as they departed" removes redundancy |
